subject: Enterprise pilot carveout + autoscale exemption request
messages:
From: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@nimbus.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-03 09:12 PDT
Subject: Pilot carveout + capacity ask for evaluation pilot

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team here at Nimbus is excited to run a 12-week evaluation of Redwood Dedicated for a multi-tenant analytics feature. Before we lock dates, we need two things confirmed on your side:

1) A temporary carveout of a small GPU pool (4x A10G equivalent) reserved for our pilot window (Sep 1 - Nov 24). We need predictable throughput for nightly batch re-ranking runs and daytime API traffic.
2) An autoscale exception that allows our pool to burst above the normal per-tenant cap for a short period during scheduled model sweeps (expect 6–8 hours, once every 3 weeks).

Attached is a draft SOW and a proposed capacity spreadsheet (pilot_capacity_plan.xlsx). Our procurement team would like an outline of the exception approval process, who signs off, and any cost/commit implications.

Can you put me in touch with the right people to evaluate?

Appreciate it —
Sarah
Director, Product Integrations
Nimbus Analytics

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@nimbus.ai>
Date: 2027-08-03 10:04 PDT
Subject: Fwd: Pilot carveout + capacity ask for evaluation pilot

Looping you in — Nimbus wants a 4x A10G carveout for Sep-Nov and an autoscale "burst" exemption for model sweeps. They also attached a SOW and capacity workbook.

Quick asks:
- Dev: is there a safe/standard way to grant a temporary carveout with predictable performance? What telemetry/SLAs can we guarantee for a pilot customer?
- Laura: what pricing / reserved commit model would you propose for a 12-week pilot that needs burst windows? Any precedent for short-term carveouts?

Sarah — ideally we can respond with a clear owner map (approval/ops), cost estimate, and a short runbook for the burst windows. cc'ing Dev and Laura to start technical + commercial assessments.

Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@nimbus.ai>
Date: 2027-08-03 14:33 PDT
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot carveout + capacity ask for evaluation pilot

Ben / Laura / Sarah —

Technical thoughts after a quick pass on the workbook:
- We can provision a tenant-scoped pool pinned to a Dedicated capacity island for the pilot dates. That gives isolation and predictable latency.
- For the "burst" exemption, we can enable a scheduled temporary override that expands the tenant's max concurrent slots for pre-approved windows. Ops will throttle to maintain cluster stability; during bursts we should expect 15-25% higher 95th latency for other best-effort tenants on the same physical cluster unless we schedule a physical carveout.
- Alternative (safer): provide the pilot a soft carveout (reserved capacity + guaranteed minimum throughput) and a paid burst lane (short-term reserved nodes).

Ask: DevOps needs SLA tradeoffs to present to the capacity team. Laura — can you confirm whether Nimbus is willing to pay a short-term reserved node premium for burst hours? If not, we need to schedule bursts during low-util windows and accept possible degradation.

I'll draft a runbook for the scheduled burst override (scheduling, alerting, automatic rollback, and owner list).

- Dev
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@nimbus.ai>
Date: 2027-08-04 09:17 PDT
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot carveout + capacity ask for evaluation pilot

Thanks — pricing position below (high level):

Option A — Short pilot carveout (recommended):
- 12-week reserved carveout: 4x A10G-equivalent nodes, billed at 40% of monthly reserved rate (pilot discount)
- Burst windows: paid burst nodes at 2x hourly of reserved nodes during scheduled sweep windows
- Minimal setup fee; 1-week lead time to provision

Option B — Soft carveout (lower commitment):
- Guaranteed minimum throughput SLA, no physical isolation; monthly billing at on-demand rates with a cap; burst events best-effort (no guaranteed latency)

Commercial asks for Nimbus: confirm which option and whether legal/procurement needs a PO vs signed SOW. If they want bursts included without a premium, we can do it as a one-off credit but need exec approval (finance + head of sales).

Ben — I can draft the short commercial summary and a PO template. Dev — please attach your runbook draft when ready.

Laura
Sr. Product Manager, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@nimbus.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-05 16:48 PDT
Subject: Re: Pilot carveout + capacity ask for evaluation pilot

Sarah — we can move forward on Option A (short reserved carveout + paid burst nodes) if Nimbus signs the SOW and issues a PO. I've attached a redline SOW (Nimbus_SOW_draft_v1.pdf) and a PO template link.

Next steps I propose:
1) Nimbus: confirm Option A and issue PO (procurement) — target by 2027-08-10.
2) Redwood: Dev to finalize runbook; Laura to produce the commercial summary and monthly estimate.
3) Provisioning lead time: 7 business days after PO & signed SOW.

If Nimbus needs the bursts included at no extra cost, I'll escalate for a one-time credit approval, but that requires signoff from Sales leadership and Finance (timeline ~48 hours).

Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
